It took me about 2 weeks to be able to type as quick as I could with qwerty, after another week I was definitely faster. The first couple of days though it was extremely difficult to type anything. I think it is worth switching for sure, you will notice the difference if you are completely used to it. But don't do it until you don't have any important projects or stuff like that.
Two weeks sounds unbelievably fast. What was your approach?

The way I did it was pretty active, I tried to type as much as I could without getting too bored. I did things like writing down what I did every day, chatting with people online a lot, sometimes even typing summaries of things I read on the internet and before I went to sleep I would write short stories about random stuff. I think that if you type a lot on a normal day it might be harder because you're more used to a qwerty keyboard, I never typed a lot before switching so that might have helped me. Also a small tip that might help is if you're looking for a letter when you just switched, really look for it, don't just have a quick look at all the letters until you find the one you're searching for, this way you'll get use dto the lay out faster.

It completely depends on your current abilities. I started using computers when I was about 6, and by the time I was in my early twenties I'd tried and failed multiple times to try and learn to touch type. I simply couldn't do it, so I always had to look at the keyboard and couldn't get above maybe 60 WPM. Dvorak is extremely natural, so I was finally able to touchtype, and now I'm bordering on 100 WPM.

For me, the difference was worth it because it was also the difference between looking at the keyboard and not, in addition to the increased speed and accuracy, not to mention lowered wrist pain. From starting off to 60WPM, it was about 2 months for me, but I typed quite a bit everyday, so YMMV.

This is something that you're going to be doing for the rest of your life. Do you really want to keep using an inefficient system every single day for the rest of your life just because that's what you grew up with? I say, be your own person, and if you find something that's better, use it. The world would be a better place if more people did that, and it all starts with you and dvorak.

I am Journalist Tim Pool. I have spent years covering conflict around the world but most recently spent several weeks exploring the California Drought. AMA!

Hey Tim, very impressed with your work over the last few years. I'm a self made journalist myself and I follow your model (yes, this is the same guy on your Reddit AMA) and was wondering what your thoughts are on the confederate flag/monument debate and free speech in general. How do you feel about the removal of the flag or even monuments from government property and what role does free speech have in businesses? At what point does curbing foul speech (hate speech) become censorship?

Its a really tough question when it comes to business, the challenge always lies with how society feels at a certain moment. Gawker was shocked at the backlash they got for their CFO story because its not the first time they've done something like this. They won't be able to survive if they follow that model so they have to change.

I think the removal of the flag makes people feel better but ultimately doesn't really solve problems. We gave Columbus a holiday and that guy was pretty much an asshole. I personally don't care if the flag is removed but I'm not from the South so my opinion means little.

Censorship is what it is whether a business or a government does it, however out 1st amendment only protects us from government intrusion. Businesses will do whatever they have to to survive which means Reddit will ban subreddits and Voat will too. If a business wants to expand to a certain size it has to accommodate more people and thus it enters the Lowest Common Denominator problem.

What do you think about the near future of drones in live reporting? Are the legal challenges surmountable with anything short of open defiance? Do you think that it will be worth the fines to put them up for a major story before the FAA says OK?

Drones are a novelty. I have flown my drone a couple times at breaking news events and we really didn't need to. Even when CNN does it the drone part is the bigger part of the headline.

What do you think about the state of journalism at the moment? The clickbaiting, sloppy reporting, many times biased reporting, etc., that even some mainstream news sources have been feeding into.

Also you seem to be out there getting your hands dirty and doing your own investigating, have you noticed many others doing the same? It seems a lot of "news" these days is just pulling from one or two other sources and putting their own spin on it depending on the audience they're appealing to.

News today is "churnalism" and it scares me. Putting your own spin on news is cool sometimes but I always try to dig a bit more into the stories people are talking about. News is made for people who aren't a part of a community so they need to be informed, however its more profitable to say, lie about video games, than it is to tell the truth because the truth isn't as exciting.

I see a lot of journalists who cover news on the ground but the funny thing is its a small enough community to where many of us know each other. Whenever I go to a conflict I can expect to see a bunch of my friends.

Failure to properly monetize. We end up with clickbait churnalism that isn't researched. Just look at what everyone wrote about Reddit and Voat, saying it was all sexist trolls.

For example i don't think our national/state news in my country is objective (anymore) and has a strong political agenda. Other news (-corporations) don't want to risk losing their advertisers with critical news items.

Yes, but can you post a proof?

Let's take 111 x 111 = 12321 as an example.

Obviously, 111 x 111 = (100 + 10 + 1) x 111 = 100 x 111 + 10 x 111 + 1 x 111.

100 x 111 = 11100

10 x 111 = 1110

1 x 111 = 111.

11100 + 01110 + 00111 = 12321.

Notice that the first decimal "seat" (English isn't my first language, don't know what it's called) appears as a zero in every instance but the last. The last decimal seat (5th one) appears as a zero in every instance but the first. The second and second-to-last appear as a zero once and a 1 twice = 2. The third seat has a 1 in all instances -> 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

The pattern here is that you'll always have a 1 as the first number and a 1 as the last number. If you have an n-amount of 1's (111 x 111 being n = 3), it gives you the pattern 1 ... n ... 1.

Don't know if this counts as a proof really but the pattern follows reason.

Edit: Only works for n = 1,2,...,9.

They're generally referred to as decimal "places".
